data.question_title: What does it mean to be an international organization?

An international organisation is defined by the United Nations as "any organisation established by a treaty or other instrument governed by international law and having its own international legal personality. An international organization may also include among its members entities other than States" (Article 2 of the Draft Articles on Responsibility of International Organizations, 2011).

data.question_title: Can you clarify what ‘pre-existing work’ means including an example?
data.answer:
The intention is to avoid "copy and paste" work that has already been funded in the current proposed form. Applicants are encouraged, however, to use previous work as a foundation for a new proposal. For instance, an expansion, implementation in a different country, a new methodology, or repurposing previously used data, would all be acceptable. Repackaging a proposal that was already accepted and funded by a different organization would not be acceptable.
